html:
Alexandria Eschate, "Alexandria the Furthest", was a city founded by Alexander the Great in 329 BCE on the Jaxartes river, the Syr Darya. It stood where the city of Khujand in Tajikistan is today.

The river marked the edge of the Persian world Alexander had conquered. Beyond it lived the nomad Saka. Alexander built the city as a frontier fort at the mouth of the rich Fergana Valley, and the ancient writer Arrian says its walls went up in about twenty days. He settled it with Greek mercenaries, Macedonian veterans who could no longer fight, and local people.

While building it he faced a revolt in Sogdia and an attack by Saka horsemen across the river. He beat them in the battle of the Jaxartes, then turned back to deal with the revolt.

It was the most northeastern of the many cities he founded during his conquests. After him it passed to the Seleucids and then the Greek kings of Bactria. Khujand later became a stop on the Silk Road and is one of the oldest cities in Central Asia.
